question: What is the primary purpose of essential drugs in a healthcare system?

options.A: To replace all traditional remedies in rural communities
options.B: To provide experimental treatments for rare chronic illnesses
options.C: To generate maximum revenue for local pharmaceutical companies
options.D: To satisfy the priority health care needs of the population

explanation: Essential drugs are specifically chosen because they target the most common and urgent health conditions affecting a community. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h1)

question: Why does limiting the number of available medicines improve a health system?

options.A: It completely eliminates the risk of patient allergic reactions
options.B: It forces doctors to prescribe only expensive imported brands
options.C: It guarantees that pharmaceutical companies stop manufacturing
options.D: It lowers costs and makes medicine supply easier to manage

explanation: Carrying fewer, well-tested drugs simplifies purchasing, storage, and distribution while keeping prices affordable. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h1)

question: In which year did the World Health Organization publish its first model list of essential medicines?
explanation: The World Health Organization introduced the very first model list in 1977 to help countries prioritize public health needs. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h2)

question: What major problem prompted the creation of the essential drugs concept?

options.A: Hospitals had too many doctors and not enough clinical space
options.B: Pharmaceutical companies refused to sell medicines to developing nations
options.C: Countries wasted money on redundant drugs while lacking basic treatments
options.D: Patients refused to take any form of modern pharmaceutical care

explanation: Early global health planners noticed limited budgets were being squandered on ineffective remedies instead of life-saving basics. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h2)

question: Which of the following is NOT a standard criterion for selecting an essential drug?

options.A: Bright packaging color and appealing flavor

explanation: Aesthetic features like color and flavor do not determine whether a drug is medically essential for public health. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h3)

question: Why is cost-effectiveness a major factor when choosing essential drugs?

options.A: It guarantees that the manufacturer makes a high profit margin
options.B: It proves that the medicine was manufactured inside the country
options.C: It ensures limited financial resources can treat the maximum number of people
options.D: It eliminates the need for any healthcare workers to monitor patients

explanation: Because healthcare budgets are always restricted, choosing cost-effective options stretches funds to cover more patients in need. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h3)

question: How does bulk purchasing of essential drugs help health ministries?

options.A: It drives unit prices down and saves money
options.B: It increases the expiration rate of supplies
options.C: It complicates the daily work of pharmacists
options.D: It forces manufacturing companies to close down

explanation: Buying large quantities of standardized medicines allows governments to negotiate better prices and conserve funds. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is a major clinical benefit for nurses and doctors who work with an essential drug list?

options.A: They can prescribe any experimental drug found anywhere in the world
options.B: They master a smaller group of drugs, leading to fewer prescription mistakes
options.C: They avoid communicating directly with patients about side effects
options.D: They never have to read medical journals or textbooks again

explanation: Knowing a concise list of reliable drugs helps clinicians understand dosages and interactions thoroughly, minimizing errors. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h4)

question: What is a common misconception patients sometimes hold about essential drugs?

options.A: They think essential drugs are only sold in overseas luxury clinics
options.B: They refuse to take them because they taste too sweet
options.C: They assume essential drugs can cure every known genetic disorder
options.D: They believe essential drugs are inferior because they are affordable

explanation: Because essential medicines are reasonably priced generics, some people wrongly assume they lack potency compared to expensive brands. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h5)

question: What administrative problem frequently disrupts the availability of essential medicines in clinics?

options.A: Too many pharmaceutical factories opening up in local towns
options.B: An excessive surplus of trained doctors in rural areas
options.C: Patients refusing to visit health facilities during dry seasons
options.D: Poor supply chain management and distribution bottlenecks

explanation: Even when drugs are budgeted for, weak logistics and transport systems often prevent them from reaching remote clinics on time. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h5)

question: What is a primary goal of incorporating essential drugs into Nigeria's national health strategy?

options.A: To restrict healthcare services only to urban federal capitals
options.B: To ensure affordable access to life-saving treatments like malaria medications
options.C: To eliminate all traditional medicine practices across every region
options.D: To promote the sale of expensive imported brand-name syrups

explanation: Nigeria's policy uses the essential medicines framework to guarantee that common deadly conditions like malaria have available treatments. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h6)

question: A rural health clinic in Nigeria runs out of basic antibiotics due to weak local distribution. Which national strategy is failing in this specific instance?

options.A: The regulation of surgical equipment manufacturing standards
options.B: The curriculum used to train primary school teachers
options.C: The Essential Drug Policy supply chain and distribution network
options.D: The enforcement of international luxury hotel taxation

explanation: Stockouts at rural clinics highlight flaws in the procurement and distribution mechanisms outlined by the national drug policy. [learn more](GNS215_U1_T2#GNS215_U1_T2_h6)
